comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PREMISE CORRECTION (epic-critical; applies to whoever drives these stories). From a second epic-driver session, verified against current origin/main.

## The cited corpus export no longer exists anywhere
Both root children quote measurements from a "rebar export 2026-08-03" and from session-workspace paths `files/parity_*.py`, `files/parity-results.md`, `files/rich-text-design-notes.md`. A full search found NONE of it: not on disk anywhere under the repo (including `.rebar/` and `.tickets-tracker/`), not in git history, and not in the tickets store. rebar has **no file-attachment store**, so those `files/…` paths were an ephemeral session workspace that is gone.

Consequently these figures are unreproducible and unauditable, and cannot be used as ACs:
- Cloud (`brutal-dyable-lion`): **5,730 bodies**, **99.65%** idempotent round-trip, 56.7% structurally rich, and the per-construct counts (headings 1,924; bullet lists 2,538; task lists 1,780; ordered 795; code 280; tables 60; blockquotes 33; rules 72; strong 1,396; inline-code 2,569; em 439; strike 7; link 12).
- DC (`repressive-delectable-swan`): **179** code-arrow bodies, **70** table-erosion bodies, **~68%** of bodies / **~78%** of chars rich, the "9115->9110 monotonic decay" body.

## The store has drifted, so the exact cardinality is unsatisfiable
The live store today holds **5,209** bodies, not 5,730. An AC asserting "the fixture holds 5,730 bodies" can never pass against a fresh export.

## A vendored full corpus cannot land anyway
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `check-added-large-files` at its default **500 KB per file**; there is **no LFS**; and `.gitignore` carries a recorded decision NOT to raise that cap. The full body set is ~5.9 MB, so "vendor the 5,730-body corpus" is blocked by the commit gate as written.

## Recommended re-scope (evidence-backed, keeps the regression value)
1. Commit a **generator script** (doctrine already exists: `scripts/capture_jira_fixtures.py` — capture, scrub, commit, then re-assert the scrub in a test).
2. Vendor a **stratified sample**: every body exhibiting the phenomenon under test, plus a random prose sample; shard so each file stays under 500 KB.
3. Replace the historical cardinalities with **counts measured from the committed fixture**, asserted exactly (so a silent regeneration still fails the test), and keep the RATIO bars as floors.

This was executed for the DC side as a working reference: `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py` produces `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/{code_arrow,table,prose}.json` = 29/29/120 = **178 bodies**, each shard <=127 KB, scrub verified (0 tenant hostnames, 0 real emails, 0 live URLs). Measured over it: 92.7% of bodies / 98.4% of chars render rich. See `/tmp/pony-swan-271c.patch` and the handoff comment on `repressive-delectable-swan`.

One further caution for the Cloud story: the DC corpus run showed pandoc-class tools silently DELETE HTML comments, and rebar's own `<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->` marker is an HTML comment. Whatever engine encodes Markdown->ADF should be checked for the same class of loss before its idempotence figure is trusted.

EPIC-LEVEL BLOCKER: three of the four remaining children cannot pass plan review as written, for a reason unrelated to their content — their descriptions exceed the 8,000-character plan-review admission limit (deterministic gate P4, "Ticket description exceeds the review admission limit"). The review fast-fails before any criterion is evaluated, so no amount of technical correctness helps until each is cut down.

Measured today:
- `disparaged-parodistic-shrew` (3388): **21,954** chars — 2.7x over.
- `emersed-specific-mutt` (789c): **20,361** chars — 2.5x over.
- `ashy-waterlog-hamadryas` (5c0e): **11,176** chars — 1.4x over.
- `dangerous-original-graywolf` (3289): 5,503 chars — within the limit.

Both already-landed children hit the same wall and had to be trimmed: `brutal-dyable-lion` needed several passes to get under (it PASSED at 7,996), and `repressive-delectable-swan` took five trims to reach 7,950 — a couple of those rounds cost a full LLM review each because the gate reports only "exceeds the limit" and the check is on the SAVED description, so an over-limit edit is not visible until the next review runs. Condense BEFORE reviewing, and leave ~100 chars of headroom rather than landing on 8,001.

What must be preserved when condensing (learned from the two that landed): every concrete anchor the reviewer verifies against the codebase — file paths, symbol names, line-number citations, config keys, ticket ids, and the named test for each AC. Cut redundancy and repeated justification prose, never the anchors, and never merge or drop an AC.

This is being handled as part of driving the epic; recording it here because it is a property of how these six tickets were authored, not of any one story, and whoever picks up the tail will hit it immediately.

compiled_state.description:
# Bidirectional Markdown ⇄ Jira rich-text sync (Cloud ADF + DC wiki)

## Problem
The reconciler routes descriptions plus comments through RichTextCodec, but Cloud encode still emits plain-text ADF paragraphs while WikiTextCodec is identity. Markdown headings, lists, checklists, code, plus emphasis therefore appear as literal source in Jira. Jira-authored rich text reads as noise when pulled into rebar. The desired result is native ADF for Cloud plus native wiki markup for Data Center without echo loops or content erosion.

The design is grounded in six experiments over the authoritative rebar export (1,801 tickets / 5,730 bodies), recorded in session log 5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5. marklas reached 99.65% idempotent Markdown↔ADF round-trip over that corpus. Jira wiki markup is lossy for punctuation-dense prose, so the DC path must not rely on codec fixed points.

## Design
Use two asymmetric codecs behind one state-based echo-safety layer on the existing adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py seam.

Cloud is fully bidirectional. Add Markdown-aware ADF functions to adf.py backed by marklas as a PINNED OPTIONAL EXTRA that is lazily imported (superseding the original vendor-under-src/rebar/_vendor/marklas plan), canonicalize combined strong+strikethrough mark order, then wire AdfCodec plus the direct Cloud send/fit/compare sites during the cutover story.

DC is a one-way Markdown→wiki renderer with bidirectional synchronization. A segmenting renderer converts structurally safe units, substitutes prose arrows before pandoc, wraps ASCII tables in noformat, plus passes dangerous units through verbatim. Missing pandoc, timeout, or pathological input falls back without data loss. WikiTextCodec remains identity until the cutover story.

Echo safety for both targets uses the existing ADR-0026 per-binding baseline plus normalize_outbound. The baseline stores the canonical remote value observed after a successful push. A change-gated fixed-size rich_sha records only real changes. Three-way baseline/local/remote comparison uses last-write-wins while always flagging concurrent edits. Origin-gated outbound preserves Jira-native constructs such as panels, mentions, plus dates.

## Sequencing
Prerequisites e369 and 3e73 are closed. Capability lands before observable cutover:

1. repressive-delectable-swan: pure DC renderer capability.
2. brutal-dyable-lion: pure Cloud ADF capability.
3. ashy-waterlog-hamadryas: DC timeout, subprocess, performance, GPL/SBOM hardening; depends on the DC renderer.
4. disparaged-parodistic-shrew: live cutover, state echo suppression, conflict detection, rollback; depends on both codec capabilities.
5. emersed-specific-mutt: append-only comment ID map plus codec-routed comment creation; depends on cutover.
6. dangerous-original-graywolf: live DC rendered-HTML harness plus cross-repo contract; depends on DC hardening plus cutover.

Descriptions cut over before comments. Both Cloud plus DC cut over only in disparaged-parodistic-shrew, together with the echo-safety mechanism, once-only re-emit, second-pass convergence proof, plus flag-gated rollback. This avoids a hazard-before-safety window.

## Child responsibilities

### DC renderer capability
Create adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py. Split bodies into blocks or list items. Render safe units through pinned pypandoc-binary. Preserve dangerous prose plus ASCII tables. Provide identity fallback when pandoc is absent. Keep WikiTextCodec plus live send paths unchanged. Test the vendored DC corpus.

### Cloud ADF capability
Add markdown_to_adf, adf_to_markdown, plus fit_markdown_to_adf_limit in adf.py. Ship marklas plus its transitive mistune as a pinned OPTIONAL EXTRA, imported lazily inside the three function bodies with ImportError routed to the plain adf.py fallback. Preserve the plain conversion functions for fallback. Keep live send paths unchanged. Test the committed Cloud corpus.

DEVIATION (operator-approved): the original vendor-under-src/rebar/_vendor/marklas plan was BLOCKED by review — marklas requires mistune, while the engine importing adf.py is contractually dependency-free (pyproject.toml line 69: engine assets are stdlib-only package data), and src/rebar/_vendor is not importable from the reconciler subprocess. Vendoring both libraries would put roughly 398 KB across 56 files inside that stdlib-only tree. The lazy-import optional extra is the only option preserving the documented contract, and mirrors the agents, metrics and grounding precedents. Vendoring stays available later. The resulting no-extras-install tolerance belongs to the cutover story disparaged-parodistic-shrew and is recorded there.

CORPUS EVIDENCE CORRECTION: the 2026-08-03 export and its files/parity artifacts no longer exist anywhere, so the quoted figures are unreproducible. Re-measured against the live store (4,996 unique bodies): idempotence reproduces at 99.75 percent, structural richness does NOT (22.8 versus 56.7 percent claimed), and the 5,730-body cardinality is stale. Both corpora are committed, scrubbed, sharded samples from committed generators, with thresholds set from measurement.

### DC robustness
Locate the wheel-bundled pandoc. Bound subprocess work per field. Kill the process group on timeout. Fall back without content loss. Add reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s to config schema, config docs, environment mapping, plus config golden. Record GPL/SBOM obligations for the bundled binary.

### Live cutover plus echo suppression
Repoint AdfCodec to the Markdown-aware functions. Wire the DC renderer into WikiTextCodec. Route both live send paths through the codecs. Preserve the plain/identity flag rollback. Persist observed-after-push baselines plus change-gated rich_sha. Compare baseline/local/remote through normalize_outbound. Flag every concurrent edit. Suppress unchanged second passes. Preserve Jira-native constructs through origin gating.

### Append-only comments
Persist local-comment-key→Jira-comment-ID mappings. Capture returned IDs on create plus update paths. Mirror only newly created comments in either direction. Do not sync edit or delete. Use the same rich-text codec as descriptions. Retain body equality only as compatibility fallback for pre-map state.

### Live DC plus cross-repo contract
Extend the Docker Jira DC harness to push rich text, read expand=renderedFields, assert rendered HTML, rerun reconciliation, plus exercise conflict safety. Pin normalize_rich_text compatibility for the agentic-dev-platform importer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cloud description Markdown encodes as structured ADF through the production codec path.
- [ ] Cloud comment Markdown encodes as structured ADF through the production comment path.
- [ ] The Cloud corpus reaches an idempotent Markdown↔ADF fixed point, including both combined-mark bodies.
- [ ] DC safe description Markdown renders as Jira wiki through the production codec path.
- [ ] DC safe comment Markdown renders as Jira wiki through the production comment path.
- [ ] The DC corpus has zero monotonic length decay over five repeated passes, including the known ASCII-table ratchet body.
- [ ] An unchanged reconcile pass adds zero committed-state entries attributable to rich-text sync.
- [ ] The git-delta cost harness remains at or below 0.07 KB per stable version.
- [ ] Every corpus case with concurrent local plus remote edits emits a conflict instead of silently overwriting either side.
- [ ] A Jira-authored panel survives the next rebar-originated reconcile pass.
- [ ] A Jira-authored mention survives the next rebar-originated reconcile pass.
- [ ] A Jira-authored date survives the next rebar-originated reconcile pass.
- [operator-attested] [ ] The Docker Jira DC job exercises the production cutover against a live Jira DC instance.
- [ ] The live DC job verifies rendered HTML through expand=renderedFields.
- [ ] The second live DC reconcile pass performs no body update.
compiled_state.title: Bidirectional Markdown ⇄ Jira rich-text sync (Cloud ADF + DC wiki)
